notes: Strong's splits this root's meaning into a literal sense ("break in pieces") and a figurative one ("harass"); Exod.15.6 (the LORD's hand "dasheth in pieces" the enemy) shows the literal sense directly, while Judg.10.8 (Israel "vexed and oppressed" by the Ammonites/Philistines) leans toward the figurative one. BDB gives the single unified gloss "shatter" without splitting these into separate senses, and "shatter" (crushing force, whether against an army or a subjugated people) reads as one sense applied to two objects rather than two genuinely distinct senses -- kept as the single requested gloss rather than expanded to a compound one.
